belief: Everyone at church has it all together but me.
origins: On Sunday morning people arrive in nice clothes, smiling, with children in order and answers ready. We see their best and compare it with our worst. Church culture can also reward looking fine, so struggles stay hidden and everyone concludes that they alone are failing.
teaches: Paul writes plainly, “All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,” and John says, “If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.” Paul also says, “We have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.” Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” The church is not a gathering of finished people. It is a gathering of forgiven people who are still being changed, and many of them are hurting more than they show.
self_statements: I am the only one who is struggling.
If I show my struggles, I will not belong.
I must be failing as a Christian.
errors: Comparing my private struggles with their public image.
Assuming that they have no problems.
Focusing on what looks good and missing hidden pain.
Feeling inadequate and concluding that I am.
questions: How much do I actually know about the lives of people at church?
What do I show to others at church, and what do I hide?
If someone else hid struggles as I do, what would that mean about them?
What does Scripture say about the condition of all believers?
What would happen if one person were honest?
Who might also be struggling and need to hear that I am?
truth: No one at church has it all together. We are all forgiven sinners, treasures in jars of clay. My struggles do not disqualify me, and honesty can free others as well as myself.
hw_truths: All have sinned, including those who look fine.
The church is for the sick, not the perfect.
log: Each week, note one moment of honesty at church and how it was received.
actions: List what you hide at church and why.
Tell one trusted believer something real.
Ask someone “How are you really doing?”
Remember that cracks let the light through.
prayer: Father, I have compared my inside to everyone else’s outside. Thank You that Your church is for sinners. Give me courage to be real and compassion for others who are hurting too. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I hide at church?
What do I really know about them?
What does Scripture say about all of us?
Who can I be honest with?
name_example: Sarah can write: “All of us fall short, and Christ welcomes all of us.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Everyone at church has it all together but me.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
